The Austin Municipal Court and Downtown Austin Community Court will hold their 2025 Warrant Amnesty program from March 31 through April 25 to help those with unpaid citations and/or outstanding warrants. Individuals who resolve active warrants will have warrant fees waived; however, they must contact the court to take advantage of this program. No officers will be sent out to take defendants into custody, and those who come to any Austin Municipal Court or Community Court location voluntarily will not be arrested. Options are available for those who are not able to pay immediately, including payment plans, community service, or hardship waivers for those who qualify. This program applies only to active cases in front of the Austin Municipal Court or Downtown Austin Community Court. In last year’s Warrant Amnesty program, 1,988 outstanding warrants were cleared, and 14,466 civil parking citations were terminated.

The program is a core part of our commitment to building trust and accountability with the public we serve,” said Clerk of the Court, Mary Jane Grubb. “We want the public to know, if they have an unresolved citation or warrant, they should not be afraid to come talk to us. Our staff can discuss options and help customers come into compliance.” There are multiple walk-in dockets scheduled Mondays through Fridays during the amnesty period. Judges and prosecutors will be available to review cases, discuss options, and issue appropriate orders. No appointments are needed during these walk-in dockets. Warrant Amnesty applies only to active cases, and all services are provided free of charge. Spanish interpreters will be available. # Find an Alternative Way To Pay the Court

If you are unable to pay a court fee, payment alternatives may be available to you. All payment alternatives must be approved by a judge. Proof of income and expenses is required, as well as two references.

---

#### 1. [File a plea](https://www.austintexas.gov/municipal-court/plead-no-contest-to-charges-in-municipal-court)

You must enter a plea in your case before any payment plan can be processed. You may plead "guilty" or "no contest." By a plea of guilty, you admit the act is prohibited by law and that you committed the act charged. A plea of no contest means that you will not dispute the charge against you. A plea of no contest may not be used against you in a future civil suit for damages.

---

#### 2. [Submit a financial affidavit](https://www.austintexas.gov/municipal-court/financial-affidavit-form)

The financial affidavit serves as a report to the court of your income, expenses, and other criteria that might affect your eligibility for alternative payment options. In the financial affidavit, you will communicate to the court how you might be able to pay. Options include:

* $75 per month or the total due to the court divided by 12 (whichever is greater). Payments are rounded up to the nearest whole dollar.
  + For example, if you owe $1,000 your monthly payment would be $1,000/12 = $84/month.
* Regular payments after an extension
* A lower monthly payment plan
* Community service (the standard rate is $12.50/hour)
* Going before a judge to discuss your particular case

A lower monthly payment plan and community service are options only given by a judge.

---

## Request jail credit

If you have been incarcerated, you may[request credit for time served](https://www.austintexas.gov/municipal-court/request-credit-for-jail-time). If you have not already entered a plea of guilty or no contest for the case(s) you are requesting jail credit for, you will be required to do so.
